# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — from-scratch prompt: "write computed values (no recalc)" contract + inspect/verify workflow
- Changes I made:
  - prompt.md (new): grading contract (data_only, no recalc → formula strings read empty; compute in Python and write literals even for "I need a formula"/VBA asks; overwrite pre-existing formula cells in answer_position with literals) → clusters A/B/C.
  - prompt.md: type/text exactness knowledge (numbers as numbers, exact sheet-name text, '#NUM!'/'#N/A' are str) → B.
  - prompt.md workflow: inspect real cells with coordinates via openpyxl (the preview hides empty leading rows), use in-sheet examples as test cases, openpyxl load-modify-save rather than a pandas round-trip → E/D.
  - task_template.md (new; all placeholders kept, validated with adapter._task_template_error=None): Inspect/Solve/Verify steps replace "once that file exists, you are done"; reopen with data_only and print the answers; finish with a no-code reply → F.
- Expected effect + safety: should fix most of A (37378, 46897, 53383, 55049, 6698, 7902, 8942), plus 267-18 and 9569/56563/55979, and 59196/227-40/50768 via the layout rules. Safe because all 18 passing tasks already wrote values (10 of them have formula goldens), so the contract codifies their behavior. The moderate risk is the pandas-to_excel passers (14) switching writer; pandas is preferred-against, not forbidden.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none (first iteration).
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: pure semantic misreads (39046, 43436, 48527, 51-12) that rely only on the generic "use in-sheet examples" nudge.
- Plateau signal: n/a.
- Focus next iteration: read the RESULT. If the A-cluster tasks still fail, check whether the agent still writes formulas (strengthen the contract) or computes wrong values (logic). Check whether any pandas passers regressed due to the openpyxl preference.

## Iteration cand_0002 — structure the "sheet/instruction as spec" step (formula-aware inspect, pre-save example check) + 3 bounded contract/knowledge rules
- Changes I made:
  - prompt.md contract: an instruction-named start cell governs placement; Sheet-Level answer_position is only the outer limit (C: 560-12).
  - prompt.md step 1: inspect snippet printing formula text and cached value; include the rows past the end of answer_position (B/F: 53647, 43436, 37456).
  - prompt.md step 2 split into bullets: examples include the instruction text; a partially filled answer range = expected output (exception: fix/transform/clear tasks); the user's original formulas name the references; label × header grid = per-label aggregate; apply only the stated criteria/priority and parse text dates; next/last row = real data; a Cell-Level blank needs a reason (A/B/D/E/F: 48527, 53647, 43436, 2768, 37456).

The partial-fill rule carries an explicit exception for transform/error-cell tasks, because scan.py showed 12 passing tasks whose pre-filled answer cells differ from gold (142-12, 382-10, 416-15, 55049, 6698, 56563, …). The other rules are condition-scoped (named start cell, threshold compare, grid layout).

  - step 2 partial-fill bullet: typed pre-filled answer cells win "even when they contradict the literal wording"; the exception now also covers 'n/a' placeholders and formula outputs (48527).

# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

## No-recalc grading contract (SpreadsheetBench, hard_no_recalc)
- What worked (cand_0001, ACCEPTED +0.375, 17 fixed): telling the agent the file is read with data_only and never recalculated, so it computes in Python and writes literals even for "I need a formula"/VBA asks. Also openpyxl load-modify-save, a coordinate-printing inspect, and an explicit Verify step.
- What didn't (cand_0001 broke 2768, 560-12): the generic workflow displaced two instruction-stated details the seed had followed (sort keys; "put from I3"). Agents anchor to the top-left of answer_position unless told that a named start cell governs.
- Promising (cand_0002, unmeasured): a formula-text inspect snippet, a pre-save print of computed vs examples, and a float tolerance for threshold counts.

## Interpretation regressions between candidates (SpreadsheetBench)
- What worked: cand_0002 (ACCEPTED +0.050) fixed 4 tasks with a formula-aware inspect, a pre-save example print and float tolerance. Its rules also displaced two interpretations cand_0001 got right: copying the expected block's header row (227-40) and the per-column comparison axis implied by "all three tie" (45635).
- What didn't: a single generic "sheet as spec" bullet does not tell the agent which way to resolve a conflict between the sheet and the literal instruction. 48527 failed in all three candidates because the agent chose the literal reading over pre-filled answers.
- Promising (cand_0003, unmeasured): state the conflict resolution explicitly (pre-filled typed cells beat literal wording); check against the stated counts; use as-of-date semantics; treat drifting formula references as a bug.

# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001
- Strategy tried: a full per-failure diagnosis (trace + init/golden cell diff for all 22 failures) before writing anything. Clustering by root cause showed that 13/22 failures share one contract misunderstanding (formula strings under no-recalc scoring), so the first edit is a contract statement with its WHY rather than many task-shaped rules. Outcome not yet known.
- Plateau/stall signal: n/a (first iteration).
- What to try next: diff the per-task RESULT against the cluster table in PROCESS.md. Clusters that did not move under a generic workflow nudge (E: semantics) probably need a different lever, such as a stronger "derive the rule from the pre-filled examples and assert it reproduces them" step, not more knowledge text.

## Iteration cand_0002
- Strategy tried: for each regression, diff the parent's trace against the SEED rollout of the same task (`rollouts/val/<id>__seed__t0.json`). It pinpointed the behaviour the new prompt displaced in minutes (seed: stated sort keys / named start cell; parent: extra sort key / answer_position corner). Cheaper and more reliable than re-reading the instruction.
- Before writing a "pre-filled cells are examples" rule, measure its blast radius mechanically: scanning all 40 tasks for answer cells where init == gold vs init != gold split them 11 vs 12 and showed the rule needs a transform/error-cell exception. Without the scan, the obvious rule would have endangered ~12 passing tasks.
- What to try next: if val plateaus at ~0.85, the remaining misses are interpretation misses with no in-sheet example. Spend the last iteration on pruning/softening and on regressions, not on more rules.

## Iteration cand_0003 (final)
- Strategy: for every regression, diff three rollouts of the same task (seed / cand_0001 / cand_0002). The passing earlier trace shows exactly which interpretation was lost. For never-solved tasks, recompute gold from init in Python under a hypothesised rule. That turns "semantic misread" into a verified one-line rule (43436, 53647) before writing it.
- Plateau: Δ fell from +0.375 to +0.050. The late gains are 1-task interpretation fixes, and each prompt change also perturbs previously passing interpretations (2 broke in cand_0002). With n=1 trial per task, the noise is comparable to the gains.
- Next time: run ≥2 trials per val task once val passes ~0.85, so a single drift doesn't read as a regression. Spend later iterations pruning and consolidating step 2 as well as adding to it.

# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## from cand_0001
- dataset.json ids are ints while task ids are strings; diagnosis scripts need str(d['id']). A small pre-built "init vs golden vs output cell diff per failing task" report would save the proposer most of an iteration's diagnosis time.
- A stale /tmp/struct.py on the runner shadows the stdlib `struct` module for any python started in /tmp; worth cleaning in the runner setup.

## from cand_0002
- The proposer cannot Read the adapter source via the Read tool (permission prompt) but can via sed in Bash; making the adapter readable (or copying `_task_template_error` + the template-fill call into ./guidance) would avoid the inconsistency. The adapter is also not importable outside the harness (`model_config` missing), so the documented "import and call _task_template_error" check needs a string.Formatter fallback.

## from cand_0003
- PROCESS.md in the new work dir was pre-filled with the PARENT's PROCESS.md (cand_0002 text), not a blank template. A proposer may mistake it for its own, or append to it. Ship a blank template instead.
- The dataset init/golden files live outside the work dir (~/.cache/capevolve-ci/spreadsheetbench-data/...). Exposing their path in INSTRUCTIONS.md, together with a per-failing-task "init vs golden vs output" cell diff, would remove most of the diagnosis time.
- rejected.jsonl is absent when there are no rejects; creating it empty would avoid a confusing missing-file error.
- The SpreadsheetBench adapter silently drops every code block after the first in a reply. The agent never learns this, and it sometimes writes "simulated" output for the dropped blocks (45635). A one-line feedback note such as "N extra code blocks were ignored" would fix this at the source, without spending prompt words on it.
- Run ≥2 trials per val task once val passes ~0.85: single-trial interpretation drift (227-40, 45635 in cand_0002) is the same size as the per-iteration gains.

# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Candidate cand_0002, iteration 2 of 3, parent cand_0001 (val 0.825, 33/40). I diagnosed all 7 failures from ./trajectories by reading each trace and diffing the init and golden workbooks with openpyxl (helpers: /tmp/ce_work/snip.py prints the coordinate, formula text and cached value; scan.py gives per-task prefilled/gold stats). For the two cand_0001 regressions (2768, 560-12) I also compared against the seed rollouts. Every failure is a capability failure. All rollouts had error=None, so there is no environment fault.

## Ranked issue list (leverage = # failing tasks it reaches)
| rank | cluster | tasks | root cause (trace evidence) | tag | lever |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A. Examples not used as test cases (sheet OR instruction text) | 48527, 51-12, 2768, 43436 (4) | 48527: D2/D3 were pre-filled with the expected answers. The agent's rule cleared D2 and left D4/D5 empty. 51-12: row 2 markers 1–4 show the count is 4. The code wrote 2, the agent's own final message reasoned 4, and it never compared the two. 2768: the instruction says "fulfil the first line with 100 pcs followed by balance 20 pcs under the second line", but the output had H11=0, H12=120. | BEHAVIORAL | STRUCTURE: step 4 prints computed vs every example before saving; the rule for a partially filled answer range is conditioned |
| 2 | B. Existing formulas never looked at | 53647, 43436 (2) | 53647: init E8:E16 hold `=IF(C8>1,E31,"")`, which references E30:E32. The agent inspected only with data_only, used C5/D5 (70/80), and got E7 wrong (gold 8.75). 43436: neighbouring column H holds `=COUNTIFS(B:B,G2,D:D,"")`, which shows per-label counts. | KNOWLEDGE | EXAMPLE: a concrete inspect snippet printing formula text and cached value; rule that the user's "original" formulas name the intended references |
| 3 | C. Explicit start cell ignored (regression from cand_0001) | 560-12 (1) | "The answer should be put from I3 with the Headers". The agent anchored the headers at I2, the corner of the Sheet-Level answer_position. The seed followed "from I3" and passed. | KNOWLEDGE (contract) | CONTRACT line: an instruction-named start cell governs; Sheet-Level answer_position is only the outer limit |
| 4 | D. Grid of label × header answered per record | 43436 (1) | The answer I2:K6 has department labels in G2:G6 and months in I1:K1. The agent wrote 0/1 per-row flags; gold has counts per department and month. | KNOWLEDGE | Add a rule: a grid cell = result for (row label, column header), usually a count/sum |
| 5 | E. Extra sort keys / text dates (regression from cand_0001) | 2768 (1) | The agent sorted by issued date, then by request del date (a mixed str/datetime column it stringified), then by Line. That served line 2 before line 1. The seed sorted on the stated keys only and passed. | KNOWLEDGE | Add a rule: apply only the stated criteria/priority; parse text dates |
| 6 | F. Boundary data just outside answer_position | 37456 (1) | Row 15 was left blank because "no next date". F16 = the next date lies just below the range, and gold row 15 = 0, 2600, 15, 20. | KNOWLEDGE | Inspect rows past the end of the range; "next/last row" means the sheet's data; a Cell-Level blank needs a reason |
| 7 | G. Float threshold comparison | 51-12 (1) | `110 >= 100*1.1` is False (110.00000000000001), so the count was 2 instead of 4. | KNOWLEDGE | Add a rule with the WHY and a 1-line idiom: use a tolerance |

## Changes made this iteration
| edit | cluster | lever | file | what |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E1 | C | CONTRACT (tighten output contract) | prompt.md "How your output is judged" (+ template step 2 "starting where the instruction says") | A named start cell governs placement; Sheet-Level answer_position is the outer limit, not the anchor. |
| E2 | B, F | EXAMPLE + restructure step 1 | prompt.md step 1, template step 1 | A 4-line snippet printing `coordinate, formula, -> cached value` from both workbooks; the inspect scope now includes the answer area and the rows past its end. This replaces the old one-liner and the "load once normally, once data_only" sentence, which it now subsumes. |
| E3 | A, B, D, E, F | RESTRUCTURE (bullets) + add sourced rules with WHY | prompt.md step 2 | Step 2 split into bullets: examples (including the instruction text); a partially filled answer range = expected output, with an exception for fix/transform/clear tasks; original formulas show the references; label × header grid; stated criteria only, plus text dates; next/last row means the real data; a Cell-Level blank needs a reason. |
| E4 | G | KNOWLEDGE + reason | prompt.md step 3 | Use a tolerance for threshold/percentage comparisons, with the `100*1.1` illustration. |
| E5 | A | STRUCTURE (ordered pre-save check) | prompt.md step 4, template step 2 | Print the computed values next to the examples before saving. If the agent's reasoning disagrees with the printed output, find the bug. |
| E6 | A | consolidate | prompt.md step 5 | The verify step now also checks against the examples in the instruction. |

The file was chosen by role. Policy and knowledge go in prompt.md (the system message, re-read every turn). The per-task ordered steps in task_template.md got only two short clauses, so the two files don't diverge. No rule was dropped: the old "load once normally / once data_only" constraint is now the snippet, and "If answer_position already contains some values, infer the rule" became the conditioned bullet E3.

## Verify (trace evidence each edit addresses) and blast radius
- **E1 / 560-12.** Verify: the trace wrote `ws['I2']='ITEM'` while the instruction says "put from I3 with the Headers"; gold has I3:J3 = headers. Blast radius: the rule applies only when the instruction names a cell. Passing Sheet-Level tasks (142-12, 382-10, 416-15, 395-36, 402-43, 7902, 227-40, 50768) either name no start cell or already start at the corner they name. Bounded.
- **E2 / 53647.** Verify: in init, `E8 '=IF(C8>1,E31,"")'` points at E31/E32, gold E7=8.75=E31, and the trace never printed the formula text. For 37456, F16 lies one row below G12:J15. Blast radius: inspection only, so it adds output and nothing else. Passing runs use 2–6 of 30 rounds. The rows-past-end clause only adds context. Bounded.
- **E3 partial-fill rule / 48527.** Verify: init D2/D3 = gold values (pre-filled examples); the trace cleared D2. Blast radius: scan.py shows pre-filled cells EQUAL to gold in 463-17, 48588, 47798, 54144, 39046, 37378, 59196, 48921, 50768, 53383, 38462; the rule reinforces what those tasks already do. Pre-filled cells DIFFERING from gold in 142-12, 382-10, 416-15, 55049 ('#VALUE!'), 6698 (G4 is the formula the user wants modified), 56563 ('#NUM!'), 267-18, 9726, 9569, 48620, 59595 ('n/a' placeholders), 7902. These are fix/transform/clear tasks or error/placeholder cells, so the exception names them ("fix, modify, transform, clear, or replace … e.g. cells showing errors or a formula the user wants changed"). Residual risk: 59595/48620/9726 have a few stale values that the agent must overwrite. For 9726 and 48620 the old value is an input that the question asks to recompute. 59595's 'n/a' is a placeholder. MODERATE; flagged.
- **E3 original-formula rule / 53647.** Blast radius: tasks with formulas near the answer (6698, 267-18, 39046, 55979) already followed those references. Bounded.
- **E3 grid rule / 43436.** Verify: G2:G6 = A–E labels, I1:K1 = months, H2 = `=COUNTIFS(B:B,G2,D:D,"")`. Blast radius: grid-shaped passing answers (7902 D3:J6, 142-12) already compute per-cell results. Bounded.
- **E3 stated-criteria rule / 2768.** Verify: the trace sort key included the 'Request del date' column (stringified); the seed sort `['Order issued Date','Line']` passed; the instruction's own example (100 then 20) contradicts the output. Blast radius: applies only to sorting and prioritizing tasks (560-12 explicit order A006, A004, A005, which it supports). Bounded.
- **E3 boundary rule / 37456.** Verify: gold has 0/16 blanks, and the trace left row 15 blank with "last date". Blast radius: "Before leaving a Cell-Level answer cell empty, find the reason in the data". 53647 has legitimately blank gold E9:E16 (the formula returns ""), and that reason IS in the data, so the rule does not force filling. Bounded.
- **E4 / 51-12.** Verify: reproduced in Python, `110 >= 100*1.1` → False, and the trace's count was 2 vs gold 4. Blast radius: only threshold comparisons. Values exactly on a threshold flip toward Excel's behaviour, and away from it nowhere. Bounded.
- **E5 / 51-12, 48527, 2768.** Verify: the 51-12 final message says "the count should be 4" after the file was saved with 2; a printed compare would have shown the mismatch. Blast radius: one extra print before the save; the round count is unchanged. Bounded.
- **Template validity:** string.Formatter fields = {answer_position, instruction, instruction_type, max_turns, output_path, spreadsheet_content, spreadsheet_path}, which is exactly required + optional, and `.format(...)` succeeds. prompt.md is read raw (`_read_capability` → read_text, never .format), so the braces-free snippet is safe.

## Deliberately skipped
- Reverting the pandas "prefer openpyxl" guidance. The 2768/560-12 regressions were not caused by it (both traces fail on ordering/placement logic, not on the writer).
- Any task-specific value (department letters, 1.1, I3, item codes). The rules are phrased generically, and the `100*1.1` float example illustrates a language fact, not an answer.
- A global "fill every answer cell" rule. Gold blanks are legitimate (53647 has 8/10 blank), so the rule is scoped to "find the reason in the data".
- Moving content into task_template.md beyond two clauses, to avoid duplicating the system prompt.

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees / parallel: none. I worked serially because the session instructions forbid the Agent tool/workflows unless the user requests them.
- Prior iterations read: prior_iterations/cand_0001/{PROCESS.md, diff.patch}, LEDGER, JOURNAL; rejected.jsonl is empty.
- Size: prompt.md went from ~800 to ~1150 words. The growth is all in structured step 2 bullets and one code snippet; there are no repeated emphasis lines and no new ALL-CAPS.

## Good things to PRESERVE
- The cand_0001 "write literal values, no recalc" contract (it fixed 17 tasks), the openpyxl load-modify-save step, the Verify step, and all placeholders.

---
